name: Mango
description: Mango represents an advanced tropical biochemical pome-drupe matrix that serves as a highly potent delivery vector for an expansive spectrum of provitamin carotenoids, proteolytic enzymes, and unique polyphenolic xanthonoids, most notably *mangiferin*. This fruit forms a complex botanical lattice optimized to preserve epithelial tissue architecture, modulate endogenous immunological cascades, and supply easily accessible cellular energy seamlessly bound to bioactive, non-starch structural polysaccharides.
macroIntro: The macronutrient architecture of raw mango pulp delivers a streamlined, fluid-dense energetic framework engineered to support rapid glycogen replenishment while utilizing structural fiber fractions to buffer the postprandial insulin arc.
microIntro: Mango houses a highly concentrated cluster of specialized, fat- and water-soluble antioxidant cofactors designed to shield cellular DNA from actinic photodamage and neutralize chronic free-radical propagation.

macroNutrients.name: Calories
macroNutrients.description: A moderate biological energy density that facilitates immediate cellular ATP regeneration while maintaining structural control over daily caloric homeostasis.

macroNutrients.name: Protein
macroNutrients.description: Provides baseline plant-derived amino acid fragments necessary to sustain the metabolic integrity and enzymatic processes of the fruit matrix.

macroNutrients.name: Total Fat
macroNutrients.description: Contains trace lipid fractions that act as essential hydrophobic lipophilic carriers, maximizing the absorption pathways of co-existing fat-soluble vitamins.

macroNutrients.name: Carbohydrates
macroNutrients.description: A complex carbohydrate assembly of natural fructose, glucose, and sucrose tightly integrated into a structural pectin lattice for modulated intestinal sugar transit.

microNutrients.name: Vitamin A (Beta-Carotene)
microNutrients.description: An exceptional reservoir of provitamin A carotenoids, fundamental for driving retinal rhodopsin regeneration and maintaining systemic mucosal epithelial integrity.

microNutrients.name: Mangiferin
microNutrients.description: A rare, structurally unique C-glucosylxanthone possessing robust iron-chelating, anti-apoptotic, and direct free-radical scavenging dynamics.

microNutrients.name: Vitamin C (Ascorbic Acid)
microNutrients.description: A potent water-soluble antioxidant dose essential for driving dermal collagen hydroxylation and optimizing macrophage phagocytic capacity.

microNutrients.name: Potassium
microNutrients.description: A critical extracellular electrolyte that regulates intracellular osmotic pressure, neural action potentials, and myocardial contraction rhythmicity.

microNutrients.name: Dietary Fiber
microNutrients.description: Composed of soluble pectins and insoluble cellulose that accelerate colon transit and act as a fermentable prebiotic substrate for eubiotic gut microbes.

microNutrients.name: Vitamin B6 (Pyridoxine HCl)
microNutrients.description: Serves as a mandatory coenzyme in amino acid transamination pathways, glycogenolysis, and the synthesis of neurotransmitters like serotonin.

healthBenefits: Deep Retinal Macular Protection: Concentrated carotenoid structures, including lutein and zeaxanthin, selectively accumulate within the ocular macula lutea, mechanically filtering high-energy blue light and mitigating long-term photo-oxidative retinal decay.

Immune Modulation via Mangiferin: Bioactive *mangiferin* downregulates pro-inflammatory cytokines (such as TNF-alpha and IL-6) and inhibits NF-κB pathways, offering systemic immunomodulatory support against environmental pathogens.

Optimization of Dermal Regeneration: The synergistic bioavailability of high-dose Ascorbic Acid and Vitamin A directly accelerates cellular turnover in the basal epidermis and fuels the structural cross-linking of dermal collagen fibers.

Metabolic Glycemic Stabilization: Despite its sweetness, the native pairing of soluble fruit fibers with specific polyphenols delays gastric emptying rates and partially blocks intestinal alpha-glucosidase enzymes, stabilizing the postprandial glucose curve.
precautionsIntro: While raw mango represents a highly therapeutic and nutrient-dense tropical asset, its rich organic chemistry and unique botanical classification require targeted dietary management.
precautions: Urushiol-Induced Allergic Potential: Mangoes belong to the Anacardiaceae family and contain *urushiol*—an allergenic oily resin heavily concentrated in the peel and sap. Physical contact or ingestion can trigger acute type IV hypersensitivity reactions, including severe allergic contact dermatitis and perioral blistering.

Fructose-Driven Glycemic Load: The high absolute concentration of free monosaccharides, specifically fructose, can strain hepatic metabolic pathways. Individuals navigating insulin resistance, metabolic syndrome, or type 2 diabetes must strictly regulate portion volumes to avoid sudden glycemic excursions.

Organic Acid Mucosal Irritation: Active reserves of volatile citric and malic acids can lower localized stomach pH, causing mechanical mucosal irritation, epigastric burning, or acid reflux in patients with active erosive gastritis or peptic ulcer disease.

Cuticular Agricultural Pesticide Accumulation: To prevent post-harvest decay during maritime transit, conventional mangoes are frequently subjected to intense topical pesticide and anti-fungal treatments. Meticulous peeling and post-peel hand washing are non-negotiable.
